+//! The laser profile operation's stored parameters (#4081): what the op
+//! keeps, as heights and plain numbers - resolved into the motion
+//! crate's `laser::LaserParams` at generation.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own parameter set over general laser-cutting
+//! practice (kerf side, leads with the pierce in the scrap, tabs as
+//! uncut gaps, pierce dwell, beam power as a fraction of the source's
+//! maximum) and RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G41/G42 and linear-only controls.
+//! The kerf side, lead and tab types are the waterjet's: the same rules.
+
+use super::height::Height;
+use super::waterjet::{JetLead, JetSide, JetTabsOp};
+use crate::path_picks::PathPicks;
+
+/// The laser profile's parameters.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct LaserOp {
+    /// The beam-off travel plane.
+    pub clearance_z: Height,
+    /// The sheet's top: the plane the cut rides.
+    pub top_z: Height,
+    /// The sheet's bottom: nothing steps down to it - a laser cut goes
+    /// through in one pass.
+    pub bottom_z: Height,
+    /// The kerf width override, mm; `None` reads the laser head tool's
+    /// diameter (its kerf width).
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    /// Post G41/G42 for the control to offset, instead of the computer's
+    /// offset path.
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    /// Outer contours counter-clockwise and holes clockwise.
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead: JetLead,
+    /// Lead-in / lead-out length, mm; 0 = none.
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    /// The kerf side of open runs.
+    pub open_side: JetSide,
+    /// `None` = no tabs.
+    pub tabs: Option<JetTabsOp>,
+    /// Cut feed, mm/min.
+    pub feed: f64,
+    /// The beam power while it cuts, percent of the source's maximum.
+    pub power: f64,
+    /// The pierce dwell, s.
+    pub pierce_time: f64,
+    /// Arcs sent as chords within this tolerance, mm; `None` keeps them.
+    pub linearize: Option<f64>,
+    /// The operation's start and exit picks.
+    pub picks: PathPicks,
+}
+
+impl LaserOp {
+    /// Structural sanity (no world): every number finite and in range.
+    /// The motion crate's door repeats the refusals by name at
+    /// generation; this is the command door's yes / no.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn is_sane(&self) -> bool {
+        let nneg = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0;
+        let pos = |v: f64| v.is_finite() && v > 0.0;
+        self.clearance_z.is_sane()
+            && self.top_z.is_sane()
+            && self.bottom_z.is_sane()
+            && self.kerf.is_none_or(pos)
+            && nneg(self.lead_in)
+            && nneg(self.lead_out)
+            && pos(self.feed)
+            && pos(self.power)
+            && self.power <= 100.0
+            && nneg(self.pierce_time)
+            && self.linearize.is_none_or(pos)
+            && self.tabs.as_ref().is_none_or(|t| {
+                t.count > 0
+                    && t.count as usize == t.at.len()
+                    && pos(t.width)
+                    && t.at.iter().all(|p| p[0].is_finite() && p[1].is_finite())
+            })
+            && self.picks.refusal().is_none()
+    }
+}

+//! The laser profile's file mirror (#4081): the op's parameters as
+//! plain keys (blank options absent, no tabs absent), on the waterjet's
+//! lead, side and tab keys. Additive - no older file names the kind, so
+//! absent keys never need a default.
+//! Provenance: our own file format (`project/mod.rs`); the names are ours.
+
+use super::*;
+
+use crate::operation::{JetLead, JetSide, JetTabsOp, LaserOp};
+
+#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct LaserDto {
+    pub clearance_z: HeightDto,
+    pub top_z: HeightDto,
+    pub bottom_z: HeightDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub kerf: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead: JetLeadDto,
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    pub open_side: JetSideDto,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub tabs: Option<JetTabsDto>,
+    pub feed: f64,
+    pub power: f64,
+    pub pierce_time: f64,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
+    pub linearize: Option<f64>,
+    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "PathPicksDto::is_empty")]
+    pub picks: PathPicksDto,
+}
+
+impl LaserDto {
+    pub(super) fn from_op(p: &LaserOp) -> Self {
+        LaserDto {
+            clearance_z: p.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: p.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: p.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: p.kerf,
+            control_comp: p.control_comp,
+            reversed: p.reversed,
+            lead: match p.lead {
+                JetLead::Arc => JetLeadDto::Arc,
+                JetLead::Straight => JetLeadDto::Straight,
+            },
+            lead_in: p.lead_in,
+            lead_out: p.lead_out,
+            open_side: match p.open_side {
+                JetSide::Center => JetSideDto::Center,
+                JetSide::Left => JetSideDto::Left,
+                JetSide::Right => JetSideDto::Right,
+            },
+            tabs: p.tabs.as_ref().map(|t| JetTabsDto { count: t.count, width: t.width, at: t.at.clone() }),
+            feed: p.feed,
+            power: p.power,
+            pierce_time: p.pierce_time,
+            linearize: p.linearize,
+            picks: PathPicksDto::from_picks(&p.picks),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub(super) fn to_params(&self) -> OpParams {
+        OpParams::LaserProfile(LaserOp {
+            clearance_z: self.clearance_z.into(),
+            top_z: self.top_z.into(),
+            bottom_z: self.bottom_z.into(),
+            kerf: self.kerf,
+            control_comp: self.control_comp,
+            reversed: self.reversed,
+            lead: match self.lead {
+                JetLeadDto::Arc => JetLead::Arc,
+                JetLeadDto::Straight => JetLead::Straight,
+            },
+            lead_in: self.lead_in,
+            lead_out: self.lead_out,
+            open_side: match self.open_side {
+                JetSideDto::Center => JetSide::Center,
+                JetSideDto::Left => JetSide::Left,
+                JetSideDto::Right => JetSide::Right,
+            },
+            tabs: self.tabs.as_ref().map(|t| JetTabsOp { count: t.count, width: t.width, at: t.at.clone() }),
+            feed: self.feed,
+            power: self.power,
+            pierce_time: self.pierce_time,
+            linearize: self.linearize,
+            picks: self.picks.to_picks(),
+        })
+    }
+}

+//! Laser profile cutting (#4081): 2D through-cuts of closed and open
+//! contours with a laser beam - the kerf offset, inner contours before
+//! the contour that frees them, straight or arc leads with the pierce
+//! in the waste, tabs left as uncut gaps, and the tight-hole rule.
+//!
+//! Provenance (public sources, behaviour only, our own words and code):
+//! - General laser-cutting shop practice: the kerf is the burnt width
+//!   of the focused beam, the cut path stands kerf / 2 off the part on
+//!   the waste side, a pierce is made in the scrap and led in, holes
+//!   are cut before the outline that frees the part, and tabs
+//!   (micro-joints) hold a part in the sheet. The same rules as the
+//!   abrasive waterjet, so this cut rides that generator
+//!   ([`crate::waterjet`]) under its own voice.
+//! - RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G41/G42 and for linear-only controls.
+//!
+//! The power is a fraction of the source's maximum (the Grbl laser
+//! mode reads it as the S word against `$30`); this module only checks
+//! and states it. Nothing here guesses: each refusal names its value.
+
+use crate::cl::Toolpath;
+use crate::geo2d::{Loop, Point2, Region};
+use crate::machining2d::GenError;
+use crate::sheet::Voice;
+use crate::waterjet::{waterjet_profile, WaterjetParams};
+
+pub use crate::waterjet::{JetTabs, LeadShape, OpenSide};
+
+/// Everything the generator reads, resolved to plain numbers (mm,
+/// mm/min, seconds, percent).
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct LaserParams {
+    /// The kerf width (the laser head tool's diameter, or the op's
+    /// override).
+    pub kerf: f64,
+    /// Post G41/G42 instead of the offset path the computer walked.
+    pub control_comp: bool,
+    /// Run outer contours counter-clockwise and holes clockwise.
+    pub reversed: bool,
+    pub lead_shape: LeadShape,
+    /// Lead-in / lead-out length, mm (0 = none).
+    pub lead_in: f64,
+    pub lead_out: f64,
+    /// The kerf side of every open run.
+    pub open_side: OpenSide,
+    pub tabs: Option<JetTabs>,
+    /// The beam power while it cuts, percent of the source's maximum:
+    /// more than 0, at most 100.
+    pub power: f64,
+    /// Seconds the beam dwells to pierce.
+    pub pierce_time: f64,
+    /// Send every arc as chords at this tolerance (mm); `None` keeps
+    /// the arcs.
+    pub linearize: Option<f64>,
+    pub feed: f64,
+    /// The beam-off travel plane, and the plane the cut rides (the
+    /// sheet top).
+    pub clearance_z: f64,
+    pub cut_z: f64,
+    /// How much coarser than the importer's promise the model is, mm
+    /// (#1053).
+    pub model_excess: f64,
+}
+
+impl LaserParams {
+    /// The waterjet generator's numbers under the laser's voice: no
+    /// abrasive, the same geometry laws.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn as_sheet(&self) -> WaterjetParams {
+        WaterjetParams {
+            kerf: self.kerf,
+            control_comp: self.control_comp,
+            reversed: self.reversed,
+            lead_shape: self.lead_shape,
+            lead_in: self.lead_in,
+            lead_out: self.lead_out,
+            open_side: self.open_side,
+            tabs: self.tabs.clone(),
+            pierce_time: self.pierce_time,
+            abrasive_delay: 0.0,
+            linearize: self.linearize,
+            feed: self.feed,
+            clearance_z: self.clearance_z,
+            cut_z: self.cut_z,
+            model_excess: self.model_excess,
+            voice: Voice::LASER,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The door: the power by name, then every number the shared
+    /// generator checks, in the laser's voice.
+    pub fn door(&self) -> Result<(), GenError> {
+        if !(self.power.is_finite() && self.power > 0.0 && self.power <= 100.0) {
+            return Err(Voice::LASER.invalid(format!(
+                "the power must be more than 0 and at most 100 % of the source's maximum (it is {})",
+                self.power
+            )));
+        }
+        self.as_sheet().door()
+    }
+}
+
+/// Cut `loops` (closed contours) and `chains` (open runs) with the
+/// beam. `part` is the material the kerf must never reach; an empty
+/// region skips that law (said in the notes).
+pub fn laser_profile(loops: &[Loop], chains: &[Vec<Point2>], part: &Region, p: &LaserParams) -> Result<Toolpath, GenError> {
+    p.door()?;
+    let mut path = waterjet_profile(loops, chains, part, &p.as_sheet())?;
+    path.notes.push(format!(
+        "laser: requested power {:.1} % of the source's maximum at {:.0} mm/min; no power record is posted yet",
+        p.power, p.feed
+    ));
+    Ok(path)
+}
+

+mod tests;

+# #4081 slice 1: the laser machine kind and the laser head
+
+The laser profile cut of #4081 comes in three slices, each a draft PR.
+This slice adds the two kinds that the operation needs. It adds no
+operation and no post.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Chosen: a `laser` machine kind, declared only.** A laser table has the
+  X/Y/Z inventory of a mill or a waterjet, so only the stated word makes
+  one (as for plasma and waterjet). It is an X/Y gantry with an optional Z
+  (the focus height), no spindle, no live tool, no coolant list and no
+  rotary axis. The words `laser`, `laser cutter` and `laser cutting` read
+  as the kind.
+- **Chosen: one door law for the two X/Y gantries.** The waterjet and the
+  laser doors are the same rules with a different kind word, so
+  `no_spindle::xy_gantry_refusals` and `Machine::xy_gantry_sane` hold them
+  once. The waterjet sentences do not change.
+- **Chosen: a laser head tool kind with the beam kerf as its diameter**,
+  rpm 0 and no corner radius, as for the torch and the waterjet nozzle.
+- **Chosen: no cutting data rows on a laser head in this slice.** A laser
+  recipe (power, pierce time, assist gas for each material and thickness)
+  would add a field to `CuttingRow`, its project DTO and its UI table.
+  Slice 2 states the power and the feed on the Laser Profile operation
+  instead. A laser head with rows is refused by name: "a laser head has no
+  cutting data rows: the laser operation states the power and the feed".
+  Dropped: plain rows (they need an rpm above 0, which a beam has not) and
+  a new recipe type now (its fields need the operation to settle first).
+- **Chosen: until slice 2, a laser machine refuses each operation by
+  name.** No family admits a laser. The create-time gate says "the setup's
+  machine is a laser cutter, which cuts only laser operations", and the
+  program check says "<op>: a laser machine admits only laser operations".
+  No built-in post serves a laser, so nothing posts. The tool law test
+  states that every operation refuses a laser head; slice 2 changes that
+  to "only the Laser Profile accepts it", as the waterjet case reads.
+- **Chosen: an original glyph** (`assets/ui/svg/tool-laser.svg`): a solid
+  head, a thin beam and a burst where the beam meets the sheet, so it
+  does not read as the waterjet nozzle. `cargo xtask icons` rasterised it;
+  the other PNGs did not change.
+- **The UI stays quiet.** The New Tool combo offers a tool kind only when
+  an operation on a selectable machine accepts it, so the laser head is
+  not offered before slice 2. The machine editor's Kind combo offers
+  `laser`, because a user can write the machine file first.
+
+## Next slices
+
+2. The Laser Profile operation on `motion::sheet` (kerf offset, side and
+   direction for each chain, leads and pierce), on DXF sketch chains.
+3. A laser post (Grbl 1.1 laser mode from the public Grbl wiki), the MCP
+   reach through `add_operation` / `edit_operation`, and the docs.

+# #4081 slice 2a: the laser profile generator in the motion crate
+
+Slice 2 of #4081 (the Laser Profile operation) is split in two. This
+part is the motion crate only: the generator and its laws. Slice 2b adds
+the app operation (type, stored params, project DTO, family, ribbon,
+UI page, MCP reach). This part does not depend on slice 1 (PR #4270).
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Chosen: the laser rides the waterjet generator under its own
+  voice.** A laser profile cut and an abrasive waterjet cut follow the
+  same rules: the kerf offset on the waste side, holes before the
+  outline that frees them, the pierce in the waste with a lead, tabs as
+  uncut gaps, the tight-hole rule, open runs on a stated side, G41/G42
+  and arc linearization. `motion::laser::laser_profile` converts its
+  `LaserParams` into `WaterjetParams` with `Voice::LASER` and calls
+  `waterjet_profile`. Dropped: a copy of the planner, the tab code and
+  the emitter (about 500 lines that two issues would then have to keep
+  equal), and a new generic "sheet profile" module (a larger move of
+  reviewed code for no change in behaviour).
+- **Chosen: `WaterjetParams` carries a `voice`.** The waterjet module
+  wrote "waterjet profile" and "waterjet:" in about 20 places. Each
+  refusal and note now reads the voice of its params. `Voice` gets a
+  `short` word for the notes (`plasma`, `wire`, `waterjet`, `laser`).
+  Each waterjet sentence is unchanged: the golden CL
+  `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` and the waterjet suites pass
+  without edits.
+- **Chosen: the pierce note names the tool.** Under the waterjet voice
+  the note is the old one (pierce time and abrasive delay). Under any
+  other voice it names the pierce time and the voice's tool ("beam and
+  dwell records are not implemented"). A laser has no abrasive, so
+  `as_sheet` sets the abrasive delay to 0.
+- **Chosen: the power is a percent of the source's maximum**, more than
+  0 and at most 100, refused by name outside that range. The Grbl laser
+  mode reads its S word against `$30` (the public Grbl wiki, "Laser
+  Mode"), so a fraction of the maximum is what a post can scale. Dropped:
+  watts (the post cannot know the source's rating without a new machine
+  field). The generator only checks the power and states it in a note;
+  no CL record carries it yet (slice 3, the laser post).
+- **Kept: the clearance plane must stand above the cut plane.** A laser
+  table without Z still needs a beam-off travel; the app (slice 2b)
+  resolves the heights, and the post (slice 3) decides what a Z word
+  means on a machine without Z.

+# #4081 slice 2b: the Laser Profile operation in the app
+
+Stacked on slice 1 (PR #4270, the laser machine kind and the laser head)
+and slice 2a (PR #4273, `motion::laser`). This slice adds the operation
+that the user creates, edits, saves and generates. The laser post is
+slice 3.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Chosen: one operation, `OpType::LaserProfile`, in its own `Laser`
+  section and `Laser` family.** Stored kind id 49 and digest tag 49,
+  appended (stored ids never move). `Family::Laser` admits only
+  `Kind::Laser`, and a laser cutter admits only that family. The ribbon
+  shows the Laser section on a laser cutter only.
+- **Chosen: `LaserOp` copies the waterjet's stored shape**, with `power`
+  (percent of the source's maximum) in place of the abrasive delay. It
+  reuses the waterjet's lead, side and tab types (`JetLead`, `JetSide`,
+  `JetTabsOp`) and their project words, because the rules are the same.
+  Dropped: a shared "sheet op" struct for the two kinds (it would move
+  the reviewed waterjet params and DTO for no change in behaviour).
+- **Chosen: the program check shares the waterjet's X/Y gantry law.**
+  `machine::waterjet::check_xy_ops` holds the family, tool kind, rotary,
+  feed-ceiling and stroke checks once; the waterjet and the laser call
+  it with their own family, tool kind and word. Every waterjet sentence
+  is unchanged.
+- **Chosen: posting and the stock sim refuse laser work by name until
+  slice 3.** The verification report says "laser posting is
+  unavailable: beam on/off records, power records and pierce dwell
+  records are not implemented", the same safety rule as the waterjet
+  (#3637). The stock sim says "laser stock removal is not judged: the
+  stock sim has no laser model". No built-in post serves a laser.
+- **Chosen: a starter laser head in the catalog**, `LZ-KERF-020`
+  (`laser_tool(0.2)`), so the empty-rack refusal names a real tool (the
+  M13.4 law) and the MCP flow can add one by name.
+- **Chosen: an original op glyph** (`assets/ui/svg/op-laser-profile.svg`):
+  an outlined head, a thin beam, sparks and the kerf gap in the sheet. It
+  differs from the waterjet nozzle and from the solid laser head tool
+  glyph.
+- **The MCP reach needs no new tool.** `add_operation` and
+  `edit_operation` read the kind and its params from the registry and
+  the project DTO, as for the waterjet. Only the `add_operation`
+  description names the laser kind.
+- **Tests join directory suites.** The op tests are in
+  `crates/app/tests/machine/laser_profile.rs` (the `machine` suite) and
+  `crates/app/tests/mcp/laser_profile.rs` (the `mcp` suite); the ribbon
+  and page tests are in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/laser_ribbon.rs`.

++++
+title = "Laser cutting"
+description = "The Laser Profile operation: kerf, cut direction, leads, tabs, power, the laser cutter it needs, and the refusals you are most likely to meet."
+weight = 8
++++
+
+This page is the reference for **Laser Profile**, the one kind in the
+**Laser** group of the [operations](@/guide/operations/_index.md) ribbon.
+For the tabs themselves and what a click picks, see that page; for what a
+refusal means in general, see [Reading a refusal](@/guide/reference/refusals.md).
+
+Lengths are in mm (inches in an inch document), feeds in mm/min (in/min),
+times in seconds, power in percent of the laser source's maximum.
+
+Blue shows the operation travel; gray shows the workpiece. The schematic is not a generated NC path and has no scale.
+
+## The machine, the tool and the post
+
+**A laser cutter.** Laser Profile needs a setup whose machine is a laser
+cutter (machine kind `laser`, see [Machines](@/guide/check-and-post/machines.md)).
+
+**A laser head.** The tool is a **Laser head**, and its diameter is the
+kerf width. The starter catalog has `LZ-KERF-020` (0.2 mm kerf). Another
+tool kind is refused ("a laser profile mounts a laser head, not a ... -
+its diameter is the kerf width").
+
+**No laser post yet.** CamCraft generates and checks a Laser Profile, but
+it does not post one in this release. The verification report names each
+laser operation: "laser posting is unavailable: beam on/off records, power
+records and pierce dwell records are not implemented". The stock
+simulation does not judge laser removal either.
+
+## Laser Profile
+
+{{ <icon name="op-laser-profile" /> }} ![Top view of the beam cutting the hole first from a pierce inside it, then the plate outline from a pierce in the scrap.](../../../operation-paths.svg#LaserProfile)
+
+**For:** cutting parts out of flat
+sheet with a laser beam: one through-cut per contour, with the kerf offset
+to the waste side, leads that start in the scrap, and holes cut before the
+outline that frees the part. The cut follows the same rules as the
+[Waterjet Profile](@/guide/operations/operations-waterjet.md).
+
+**Picks:** the closed contours and open runs to cut, on the Geometry tab.
+Without picks it cuts the through-silhouette of the model.
+
+| Tab | Setting | Default |
+|---|---|---|
+| Geometry | Kerf width | Laser head: the laser head's diameter |
+| Geometry | Compensation | In computer (offset path); or In control (G41/G42) |
+| Geometry | Direction | Outer CW, holes CCW; or Reversed: outer CCW, holes CW |
+| Geometry | Open run side | On the centre line |
+| Geometry | Send arcs as lines | off (line tolerance 0.01 when on) |
+| Heights | Clearance (beam off) / Top of sheet / Bottom of sheet | from the setup |
+| Passes | Hold with tabs | off |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Lead shape | Arc |
+| Lead in / Lead out | Lead-in length / Lead-out length | 2 / 1 |
+| Feeds | Cut feed | 600 |
+| Feeds | Power | 50 % |
+| Feeds | Pierce time | 0.5 |
+
+**Kerf.** The path is the beam centre: each cutting move stands half the
+kerf off the part on the waste side. One through-cut is made at the sheet
+top; there are no depth steps.
+
+**Power.** The power is a percent of the source's maximum: more than 0
+and at most 100. The page names a power out of that range, and the
+command refuses it.
+
+**Feeds.** State the power and the feed for the material and the sheet
+thickness from the source's cut data. The defaults are only a start.
+
+**Common refusals:** "laser profile: no contour to cut"; "laser profile:
+the power must be more than 0 and at most 100 % of the source's maximum
+(it is ...)"; "laser profile: the kerf width must be a positive number
+(it is ...)"; "laser profile: the sheet's bottom (...) stands above its
+top (...)".
